or call 310-663-1340. Describe a substantial collection in advance and discuss payment by cash, bank wire or business check. Our
first-evaluation guide
explains what to expect during the visit.
Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Gold in Los Angeles
Where is the best place to sell gold in Los Angeles?

The best choice depends on what you’re selling. Look for an established buyer who specializes in the type of item you have, clearly explains the evaluation, and allows you to understand the offer before making a decision.
How much is my gold worth today?

Your gold’s value depends on its purity, weight, the current gold market price, and potentially its condition, brand, gemstones, or collectible value. Because gold prices change, an in-person evaluation provides a more current estimate.
Is 14K gold worth selling?
Yes. Although 14K gold is not pure gold, it contains a substantial amount of gold and can have meaningful value depending on its weight and current market conditions.
Can I sell gold without a receipt?

Ordinary gold jewelry can often be evaluated without its original purchase receipt, although identification or other documentation may be required for the transaction. Special pieces may benefit from certificates, grading reports, receipts, or other provenance documentation.
Should I clean my gold before selling it?

Usually, extensive cleaning is unnecessary when an item is primarily being evaluated for its precious-metal content. Avoid aggressive cleaning methods that could damage gemstones, finishes, antique pieces, or collectible jewelry.
Can I sell broken gold?
Yes. Broken gold jewelry can still have value because its precious-metal content remains valuable even when the item is no longer wearable.
Get Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles
Selling gold should not require guessing what your jewelry is worth.
Understanding purity, weight, current gold prices, and the type of item you’re selling can help you evaluate an offer more confidently.
If you have gold jewelry, broken gold, coins, bullion, estate jewelry, or other valuables you’d like evaluated,
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
can provide an in-person evaluation in Los Angeles.
Bring your items in, learn how they’re evaluated, and decide whether the offer is right for you.

children.text: Start with the items you want to sell

Place the pieces you may sell separately from anything you intend to keep. For a collection, make a short item list: a loose oval diamond, a solitaire ring, a pair of earrings or an eternity band. Use descriptions you know rather than estimated grades.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural, cut and polished diamonds only. Any size and any shape are welcome, whether loose or set in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown diamonds, rough material or uncut crystals. Our
large-diamond guide
covers substantial individual stones and multi-stone jewelry.
Keep complete jewelry and matching components together

Bring matching earrings, necklace components, removed bracelet links and accessories you already have. Note missing parts. An offer for a complete design may cover more than the single stone you first intended to discuss.

Leave stones in their settings until you have discussed any proposed work. If a stone is loose or a clasp is damaged, keep the item in its own suitable container and point out the condition. Do not undertake polishing, repairs or stone removal solely to prepare for an initial conversation.
Match each document to the correct diamond

Gather grading reports, receipts and repair records. Put a copy of the relevant document with each item on your list. A box or a familiar-looking certificate is useful context, but the actual document still needs to be matched to the piece.

Separate identification, quality and money
First establish what the stone is.

Next, consider the stone's quality information.
The 4Cs

help describe diamonds, while the condition of the actual item and the details of its setting still matter. Keep an individual diamond's weight separate from the total weight in an entire bracelet or ring.
Finally, discuss a purchase amount for the item.
An appraisal and a grading report have different purposes

Make the evaluation conversation specific

Explain whether you are considering the whole collection or selected pieces. Ask which items a proposal includes and what information remains uncertain. If further testing or alteration is suggested, discuss its purpose and arrangements before agreeing.
Does the offer include the mounting and all accent stones?

children.text: Ask for a purchase offer for your gold
A pawn shop may buy an item outright or lend money against it. Start by saying which transaction you want. The
CFPB’s financial-products guide
explains that a pawn loan uses an item as collateral. A loan amount and a purchase offer therefore answer different questions.

If your goal is to sell, record the amount you would receive for transferring ownership of the listed items. Do not compare that figure with a loan advance, an insurance appraisal or an online advertisement for a different piece.
Prepare one consistent collection for each evaluation

Photograph your pieces and make a simple inventory before visiting buyers. Separate chains, bracelets, rings, coins and loose items into identifiable groups. Note broken clasps, missing stones and any marks you can read; leave uncertain details marked unknown.

title: What Does 14 Karat Gold Mean? Marks, Color & Construction

body.alt: Ornate heavy yellow-gold bangles with colored accents
body.caption: Ornate heavy yellow-gold bangles with colored accents. Representative editorial image; not a record of this business’s inventory, staff, prices or verified material grades.

children.text: Read karat as a fraction, not a weight
14K does not mean a ring contains 14 grams of gold. It describes the nominal proportion in the alloy. The
World Gold Council's purity table
connects karat descriptions with common fineness markings.
At nominal 14/24 purity, 12 grams of verified alloy contains seven grams of gold. That calculation assumes the 12 grams is the applicable alloy weight, excluding stones and other components.
Know what a 585 mark is claiming

585 expresses 585 parts gold per thousand, or 58.5%. Nominal 14/24 arithmetic gives about 58.33%; avoid silently treating different rounded inputs as exact measurements. The actual item still needs evaluation.

Look near a clasp or inside a band for clues, but do not conclude that an unmarked piece is worthless or a marked one is authentic. Repairs, mixed components and surface layers can require closer inspection.
Color and purity describe different characteristics

Yellow, white and rose gold can all be made at 14K. The other metals and any surface finish affect appearance. A pale color is not proof that a ring is platinum, and a warm color is not proof of a higher karat.

body.alt: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools
body.caption: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools.

children.text: See our
white and yellow gold comparison
for finish and resale questions. If a particular alloy ingredient matters to you, ask the maker rather than inferring the full composition from the karat.
Distinguish hollow construction from plated material

A hollow chain can be made of a genuine gold alloy while weighing less than a similar-looking solid chain. A gold-plated piece has a surface layer over another material. These are different descriptions, as the
FTC's jewelry guide explains
Heft and magnetic response are not sufficient to identify an entire item. Have uncertain pieces assessed instead of relying on a home test. Our
testing guide
covers what measurements can establish.
Inspect the actual design and condition

A 14K label does not guarantee secure prongs, an unworn band or suitability for every activity. Construction, alloy, thickness, use and prior repairs all matter. Keep care questions specific to the maker, finish and any stones in the piece.
For a substantial necklace, the
14K chain guide
covers links and clasps. For a value estimate, use our
14K per-gram guide
and check the current reference rather than an undated article price.
Have your 14K jewelry evaluated
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys 14K jewelry, scrap and Cuban chains, with or without diamonds. Large collections are welcome.
Arrange an evaluation
in Downtown Los Angeles and discuss cash, bank wire or business-check payment.

title: Platinum vs White Gold: Alloy, Finish, Care & Resale

body.alt: Two substantial white-metal rings with large step-cut diamonds
body.caption: Two substantial white-metal rings with large step-cut diamonds. Illustrative editorial image; not actual inventory or evidence of gemstone identity, purity, coin denomination or geographic origin.

children.text: Read the full metal description
Platinum and white gold can look similar, but they are different material descriptions. The
FTC’s precious-metal jewelry guide
explains how purity is expressed. A 950 platinum description refers to 95 percent platinum, while 18K gold describes 75 percent gold in the alloy.
The
World Gold Council explains white gold

as gold alloyed with white metals, usually with a rhodium finish. The alloy and the coating should be considered separately. Ask what the piece is made from and which surface treatment, if any, is present.
Compare the questions that affect ownership

body.alt: White-metal solitaire ring worn on a hand
body.caption: White-metal solitaire ring worn on a hand.

cells: Ask for platinum fineness and alloy details
Ask for gold karat and alloy details
Identify polish, texture or any applied coating
Establish whether there is rhodium plating
Discuss condition, sizing and setting repairs
Discuss those repairs and any finish maintenance
Obtain an equivalent quote for comparison

children.text: Try the actual rings if buying. Compare fit, band dimensions and the height of the setting. A similar outline does not mean that two rings have the same metal weight, workmanship or comfort.
Avoid universal durability and maintenance promises
GIA’s platinum-alloy guidance

explains that different alloys have different working properties and that compatible materials matter for repairs. That is a reason to ask about the specific ring, rather than assuming every platinum piece behaves identically.
GIA’s ring-material guide
discusses platinum patina and notes that some manufacturers rhodium plate platinum too. Platinum should therefore not be described as universally maintenance-free or never coated.

For either metal, ask how the finish and stone setting should be inspected and maintained. Wear patterns, construction and previous work affect the discussion. Obtain advice for the particular item instead of assuming that all white gold needs replating on a fixed calendar.
Compare full quotes instead of permanent price rankings

A finished ring price includes more than its metal. Design, workmanship, stones, brand and seller terms affect the quote. If you want a meaningful comparison, request the same stone and comparable dimensions in the two metals, then identify any differences in what is included.

Ask for current sizing, repair and refinishing estimates where relevant. Record whether a service is included or charged separately. Avoid a long-term cost calculation built from invented maintenance intervals and assumed prices.
Evaluate an existing piece for resale

A resale discussion needs the actual composition, relevant metal weight and condition. Any diamonds or other stones must be distinguished from metal-content arithmetic. Ask whether the offer covers the complete piece and how its design or supported maker attribution was considered.
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.
Contact us
at 310-663-1340 to describe your precious-metal jewelry and arrange an evaluation. For gold pieces, review our
gold jewelry buying service
and the
white gold diamond ring guide
Is platinum always worth more than white gold?
No fixed ranking establishes an offer for finished jewelry. Compare the identified metal content, complete item and actual transaction terms using current information.
Can I identify either metal from color alone?
No. Similar surface appearances can hide different alloys or finishes. Records and examination are needed to establish what the piece contains.

children.text: Identify what you have before estimating a price
GIA describes diamond as a material composed of carbon
with a particular crystal structure. For an owner, the practical first question is whether an unfamiliar stone is a diamond and what is known about its origin and condition.

Describe the item as you know it: a ring, a loose stone, earrings or a necklace. If a family member called it a diamond but there is no supporting record, explain that uncertainty. A visual sparkle or fog test is not enough to establish identity, natural origin or value.
Collect the quality information that is already available
GIA’s four quality factors

are cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Shape describes the outline, such as oval or round; cut quality concerns how the stone has been fashioned. Carat measures weight and should be read alongside the stone’s millimeter dimensions.

body.alt: Round faceted diamond held in tweezers
body.caption: Round faceted diamond held in tweezers.

children.text: Do not assume every diamond should be described by the same color terminology. Our
report and grading chart guide
explains the context needed to read the fields. If no report is available, ask what can be established through examination instead of assigning grades yourself.
Keep different documents in their proper roles

cells: The information recorded about the examined stone
The original transaction and item description
A value assigned for its stated purpose and date
Known alterations, replaced parts or work performed
The proposed amount and purchase conditions

children.text: GIA explains the difference between grading and monetary appraisal
. Keep the purpose of each document clear, and ask the evaluator to match the records to your actual item. A paper associated with a jewelry box may concern another piece.
Present the complete piece or collection

Bring jewelry intact, including matching earrings, detached parts and any original supporting documents. Keep loose stones individually contained. Note known chips, repairs and replacement stones without trying to repair or dismantle the item yourself.

If selling gold and diamonds together, ask how the relevant metal weight and the stones are considered. Do not count a complete ring’s weight as pure gold or add a separate metal estimate to an offer that already includes the setting. Keep any luxury watches or attributed designer pieces identifiable within a larger collection.

title: 14K White Gold Diamond Rings: Metal, Finish & Resale Evaluation

body.alt: Substantial white-metal bezel ring with a large round diamond
body.caption: Substantial white-metal bezel ring with a large round diamond. Illustrative editorial image; not actual inventory or evidence of gemstone identity, purity, coin denomination or geographic origin.

children.text: Read the metal description before comparing rings
White gold describes a gold alloy, not a separate precious metal. According to the
FTC’s jewelry buying guide
, 14K means 14 parts gold and 10 parts other metals, out of 24. That is approximately 58.3 percent gold by weight.
The
World Gold Council’s gold jewelry guide

lists the common 583 and 585 fineness designations alongside 14 karat. It also explains that white gold is alloyed with white metals and usually receives a rhodium finish. Read the complete description rather than assuming that a bright white surface establishes the underlying metal.
Distinguish a finish from the ring’s construction

Ask whether the ring is white gold throughout or has a plated base, and have unclear markings checked. A surface coating and a gold alloy setting are different things. Photograph marks inside the band if they are readable, but treat them as information for examination rather than proof that testing is unnecessary.

Look at the shank, prongs and the area underneath the center stone. Note thinning, bent parts, missing stones, previous sizing and repairs you know about. Ask a jeweler to assess a loose stone or damaged setting before continued wear. A karat number alone does not tell you how a particular ring was made or its present condition.

cells: What does examination establish about the metal?
Is there rhodium plating, and what condition is it in?

children.text: Evaluate the natural diamond separately
The metal purity does not grade the diamond. Use
GIA’s four quality factors
to understand the reported cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Our
4 Cs guide
explains how to turn those details into questions about the actual stone.

children.text: For a multi-stone ring, identify whether a stated weight concerns the center diamond or all the diamonds together. Ask what can be established while the stones remain mounted and what is estimated. Bring any existing report, and tell the evaluator about chips, replacement stones or other changes you know about.
Separate metal-content arithmetic from a complete offer

The scale weight of a finished ring includes its stones and any other components. It should not automatically be used as the weight of 14K gold. Once the relevant metal weight and purity are established, they help describe the gold content; they do not quote the purchase price of the finished ring.

Ask how the buyer considered the natural diamond, setting, condition and any supported maker attribution. If the offer is for the complete ring, do not add a separate theoretical metal amount to it as though the setting had been excluded. Our
diamond resale offer comparison guide
helps clarify what an amount includes.

Is 14K white gold the same as platinum?
No. They are different metal descriptions. A similar white appearance does not make their composition, markings or valuation interchangeable.
Can I price my ring from its stamp and total weight?
Those details are only a starting point. The metal needs evaluation, stone weight must be distinguished, and the natural diamond and complete ring need their own assessment.

title: Choosing a 14K White Gold Engagement Ring: Setting & Care

body.alt: Heavy white-metal engagement ring with a large pear-shaped diamond

children.text: Know what 14K white gold tells you
According to the
World Gold Council’s jewelry guide

, 14K gold is approximately 58.3% gold combined with other metals. White gold is an alloy, often finished with rhodium. Two rings with the same karat can still differ in alloy recipe, construction and surface finish.

Ask the seller to identify the setting material and finish in writing. If you have a known metal sensitivity, ask about the actual alloy rather than treating the words “white gold” as an assurance of suitability. For a broader material comparison, read our
platinum and white gold guide
Examine the setting as a structure

Look at the ring from above, from the side and beneath the center stone. Discuss prong condition, the thickness of the band, how high the stone sits and how the ring fits beside a wedding band. A low profile, halo or narrow band changes the design questions; a single karat number does not answer them.

body.alt: Yellow-gold-tone and white-metal diamond bands
body.caption: Yellow-gold-tone and white-metal diamond bands.

cells: How is this particular stone supported and inspected?
Is the size comfortable, and is future resizing practical?
What care does this setting require?
Is it rhodium plated, and what service is recommended?

children.text: Do not infer that every 14K setting is stronger than every 18K setting. The actual alloy, design, manufacture, wear and repairs all deserve attention. A worn prong needs examination regardless of the ring’s original specifications.
View the diamond in the complete ring
GIA explains how setting metal affects diamond color appearance
through reflected surroundings. View the ring in more than one ordinary lighting condition. A bright display light or photograph may not show how the piece looks on your hand.
Keep appearance separate from documented diamond grades. Compare the
diamond’s 4Cs
, dimensions and report details alongside your visual preferences. Ask whether a quoted carat weight refers to the center stone or all the diamonds combined.
Plan care around the actual jewelry
There is no universal replating deadline for every wearer. Ask about the finish and have wear assessed when necessary.
GIA’s jewelry-care guidance
discusses cleaning, chemicals and storage; the appropriate approach depends on the materials and condition.

Keep purchase and service records. Before choosing a ring, clarify any resizing, inspection, repair and return terms directly with its seller. An attractive retail presentation does not establish its future resale amount.

Use our
diamond-selling decision guide
to prepare your piece. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.
to discuss an evaluation. We buy natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape; payment options are cash, bank wire or business check.
Does a 14K mark tell me the ring never needs repairs?
No. It describes gold content, not the ongoing condition of prongs, joints or other components.
Will rhodium plating change a diamond’s recorded grade?
No. The setting can influence the stone’s appearance, but a surface finish is not a new diamond grading result.

children.text: Separate the gold alloy from its surface finish
10K describes the proportion of gold: 10 parts out of 24, or approximately 41.7 percent. The
World Gold Council’s purity guide

explains how alloying changes gold’s color and lists the 417 fineness mark for 10 karat. White gold is usually finished with rhodium, so its surface appearance is a separate question from its gold content.
Ask for the full metal description. A white gold alloy ring and a ring with a coated base metal are different products. The
FTC’s precious-metal jewelry guide
helps distinguish alloy, plated and filled descriptions. Neither a bright surface nor a photograph establishes which construction you have.
Compare designs by their practical details

A plain band, a twisted design and a diamond-accent ring serve different preferences. Compare comfort and construction instead of assigning every example of one style a higher quality rating. If buying, try the actual ring and ask about sizing before paying for a design that may be difficult to alter.

Ask the jeweler what finish is present and how it should be maintained. There is no useful universal promise that every ring needs refinishing at the same interval or will last a fixed number of years without repairs.

title: Diamond Carat Weight: Points, Grams & Total Weight Explained

body.alt: Three large faceted stones arranged on a wooden surface
body.caption: Three large faceted stones arranged on a wooden surface. Representative editorial image; not a record of this business’s inventory, staff, prices or verified material grades.

children.text: Convert carats, points and grams
GIA defines a metric carat as 200 milligrams
. One hundred points equal one carat, so a “75-point diamond” weighs 0.75 ct. The following are unit conversions, not price estimates.
To convert carats to grams, multiply by 0.2. To convert points to carats, divide by 100. Keep the unit beside the number when comparing documents; “0.75” without a unit is incomplete information.
Distinguish the center stone from total carat weight
GIA explains total carat weight
as the combined weight of the diamonds in a piece. A listing for a one-carat-total-weight ring does not necessarily describe a one-carat center diamond.

For example, a ring with a 0.70 ct center diamond and 0.30 ct of smaller diamonds has 1.00 ct total diamond weight. The center remains 0.70 ct. This arithmetic does not make the ring equivalent to a solitaire containing one 1.00 ct diamond.
Ask for the center-stone weight and the combined side-stone weight separately. If the item includes colored gemstones, ask exactly which stones the stated total includes.
Use millimeter measurements for visible size

Weight and face-up dimensions are different measurements. Two stones can weigh the same while having different lengths, widths or depths. Compare the millimeter measurements on their reports rather than relying on a generic carat-to-diameter picture.

body.alt: Round faceted diamond held in tweezers
body.caption: Round faceted diamond held in tweezers.

children.text: A stone’s proportions also matter. Greater depth can add weight without providing the face-up dimensions you expect. View the actual jewelry alongside its measurements; neither the weight nor a zoomed product photograph tells the whole story.
For rounds, the
round brilliant comparison guide
connects measurements with the other report fields.
Ask whether the weight was measured or estimated

A loose diamond can be weighed independently. A mounted piece presents a different question because the setting and other stones are also present. Ask whether its stated diamond weight comes from an existing report, a prior record or a current estimate.
GIA’s appraisal guidance
identifies estimated mounted-stone weight as an example of an assumption that should be disclosed. Record that limitation instead of repeating an estimate as an exact measurement.

Bring the jewelry intact. Before authorizing stone removal, discuss why it is needed, the condition of the setting and who would perform the work. A kitchen scale reading for an entire ring is not the center diamond’s carat weight.
Keep weight separate from a purchase amount

A price per carat is meaningful only alongside the actual stone description and the transaction it refers to. Do not multiply a retail listing for a different stone by your diamond’s weight and treat the result as a purchase offer.
Compare the other
diamond quality factors
, report information, condition and any jewelry included in the sale. A larger weight does not create a guaranteed price multiple, future appreciation or a deadline to sell.
Organize the weights before a Downtown LA visit

Make a short list of the items and attach copies of the matching documents. Separate a confirmed loose-stone weight from a total-weight description or an estimate. This makes it easier to discuss several rings, loose stones or a larger collection without mixing their records.

Are carat and karat the same?
No. Carat is a gemstone weight unit. Karat describes the gold proportion of a gold alloy. Keep the stone weight and the metal description separate on your item list.

title: The 4 Cs of Diamonds: Questions to Ask Before Buying or Selling

body.alt: A large round polished diamond held in jeweler tweezers
body.caption: A large round polished diamond held in jeweler tweezers. Representative editorial image; not a record of this business’s inventory, staff, prices or verified material grades.

children.text: Start with four different questions
Use
GIA’s four quality factors

to organize the discussion: how the diamond was cut, its color description, its clarity characteristics and how much it weighs. There is no single combined 4Cs score that gives every diamond a fixed price.
Cut:
how the cutting and proportions contribute to appearance.
Color:
the reported color grade or description.
Clarity:
the internal and surface characteristics considered in grading.
Carat:
the weight of the diamond.
Write down these fields for each stone you are considering. Leave unknown information marked as unknown instead of filling the gap with a sales phrase such as “premium quality.”
Look at cut through the actual diamond

Shape and cutting style describe what kind of stone you are viewing. Cut quality concerns how it is fashioned. Two round diamonds with similar weights may still show different patterns of brightness and contrast.

Compare stones in the same lighting and viewing position, then ask to see them under another ordinary lighting condition. Record what you prefer rather than assuming that one sales label guarantees the appearance you want. For a round brilliant, our
cut-comparison guide
explains which report fields to compare.
Use the color grade without making assumptions about visibility
GIA describes color grading under controlled lighting
. Your impression when viewing a mounted ring is a separate observation. Ask to compare the actual items instead of accepting a promise that a particular range of grades always looks identical.

body.alt: Existing diamond color scale diagram
body.caption: Existing diamond color scale diagram.

children.text: If a warmer appearance appeals to you, say so. If you want a less visible tint, compare that preference against the complete piece and its price. A universal recommendation to buy one color grade cannot account for every person, stone or setting.
Ask what the clarity grade means for this stone
Clarity is more than the number of visible dots on a diagram.
GIA considers several characteristics under magnification
. Ask which features are present in the diamond you are viewing and whether any deserve closer attention.

Do not treat “eye-clean” as a laboratory grade or assume that every SI1 or VS2 diamond will look the same to you. View the actual stone and ask the seller to point out the feature being discussed. Keep appearance, the written grade and any condition concern as separate notes.
Separate carat weight from the size you see
Carat measures weight. For visible size, compare the reported millimeter dimensions as well. A ring’s total diamond weight is also different from the weight of its center stone. The
carat-weight guide
includes examples of both terms.
When comparing two rings, ask for the center-stone weight, the side-stone total and the metal description separately. This avoids comparing a multi-stone total with a single-stone listing.
Compare the paperwork and the transaction
A sample GIA natural-diamond report

shows the information to look for. Check the report type, identification and measurements; ask how the document is matched to the item. The report’s scope matters, and a general grading report does not answer every sourcing or ownership question.

For a purchase, also read the return conditions and complete item description. For a sale, ask for an offer for the exact item being presented, including its setting and any accent stones. A retail asking price or earlier insurance value is not the same as an offer to buy it today.
Prepare a diamond evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles
Bring your item intact, with existing reports, receipts and repair records. You do not need to assign grades yourself before contacting
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
. Explain any missing paperwork and ask what the evaluation can establish.
We buy natural polished diamonds of any size and shape. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Visit 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.
Arrange the visit
and discuss payment by cash, bank wire or business check before accepting a purchase offer.
Which C should I prioritize?

Start with your purpose and what you observe in the actual item. For buying, compare your preferences against complete descriptions and prices. For selling, ask the buyer to explain the factors affecting the offer rather than choosing one grade in isolation.
Do excellent grades guarantee a profitable resale?
No. Quality descriptions do not establish a future buyer, price or return. Keep the report information separate from the terms of any actual transaction.

title: How Gold Is Valued: Weight, Purity & Purchase Offers

body.alt: Gold rings, broken bracelet links and chain separated in sorting dishes
body.caption: Gold rings, broken bracelet links and chain separated in sorting dishes. Illustrative editorial image; not actual inventory or evidence of gemstone identity, purity, coin denomination or geographic origin.

children.text: If you’re thinking about selling gold in Los Angeles, one of the first questions you may have is:
How is gold valued?
The value of gold jewelry is generally influenced by several factors, including its
gold purity, weight, current gold market price, and the type of item being evaluated
. Some jewelry may also have additional value because of its brand, craftsmanship, gemstones, condition, or collectibility.
Understanding these factors before you sell can make it easier to evaluate an offer and ask the right questions.
At
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
, we believe sellers should understand how their valuables are evaluated before deciding whether to sell.
What Determines the Value of Gold?
When evaluating gold, buyers typically consider several important factors.
These include:
Gold purity or karat
Weight
Current gold market price
Whether the item is solid gold, plated, or another type of material
Refining or resale considerations
Condition and design
Brand or collectible value
Diamonds or other gemstones
For ordinary gold jewelry being purchased primarily for its precious metal content,
purity, weight, and the prevailing gold price are especially important
What Does Gold Karat Mean?
Gold karat describes how much pure gold is contained in an alloy.
Pure gold is 24 karat. Jewelry is often made by combining gold with other metals to improve durability or achieve different colors and characteristics.
The
FTC explains
that an 18K item consists of 18 parts gold and six parts other metal, while a 14K item consists of 14 parts gold and ten parts other metal.
How Pure Is 24K Gold?
24K represents essentially pure gold.
Because pure gold is relatively soft, jewelry is frequently made using lower
karat alloys rather than 24K gold.
How Pure Is 22K Gold?
22K gold contains approximately
91.7% gold
It is commonly seen in certain types of jewelry and gold coins.
How Pure Is 18K Gold?
18K gold contains
75% gold
The remaining 25% consists of other metals used in the alloy.
How Pure Is 14K Gold?
14K gold contains approximately
58.3% gold
It is one of the commonly encountered gold purities in jewelry.
How Pure Is 10K Gold?
10K gold contains approximately
41.7% gold
Because the gold percentage is lower than in 14K or 18K jewelry, two items of identical weight can have substantially different gold content.
How Do You Identify the Karat of Gold Jewelry?
Many pieces of jewelry contain a quality mark indicating their gold content.

body.alt: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools
body.caption: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools.

children.text: You may see markings such as:
For example,
generally corresponds to approximately 58.5% gold, while
corresponds to 75% gold.
However, a stamp alone should not always be treated as conclusive proof of an item’s composition.
A professional evaluation may include testing to confirm the actual precious metal content.
The
FTC provides consumer guidance
about gold quality marks and how they communicate the amount of gold in jewelry.
Why Does Gold Weight Matter?
Once the purity of an item is established, its weight becomes another major part of determining its underlying gold content.
In simple terms, an item containing more actual gold generally has a higher underlying metal value than an otherwise comparable item containing less gold.
However, sellers should understand
what exactly is being weighed
A piece of jewelry may contain:
Gold
Diamonds
Gemstones
Clasps
Springs
Other metals
Non metal components
These components can affect how the total weight relates to the actual amount of gold.
What Is a Troy Ounce?
Gold markets commonly quote precious metals using
troy ounces
, rather than the ordinary avoirdupois ounces Americans commonly use for everyday goods.
One troy ounce is approximately
31.103 grams
, according to
NIST
This distinction is important because a standard ounce and a troy ounce are not the same measurement.
You may also encounter gold buyers using grams or pennyweights.
When receiving an evaluation, ask which unit of measurement is being used.
What Is the Gold Spot Price?
The
spot price of gold
is a market reference for gold.
Gold prices fluctuate as markets change, so the price you see today may differ from the price on another day.
The
World Gold Council provides gold spot price information
and notes that the gold market also uses benchmarks such as the LBMA Gold Price.
This market price is an important starting point for understanding gold value—but it does
not automatically equal the amount a buyer will pay for your jewelry
Why Isn’t My 14K Jewelry Worth the Full Gold Spot Price?
This is one of the most important concepts for gold sellers to understand.
The quoted gold price generally refers to gold at a specified market standard. Your jewelry may contain considerably less than 100% gold.
For example, 14K jewelry contains roughly 14 parts gold out of 24.
So if you have a 14K bracelet weighing 20 grams, you should not simply multiply all 20 grams by the market price of pure gold per gram and assume that is what a buyer should pay.
The actual gold content first needs to be considered.
The buyer may then account for additional factors involved in purchasing, processing, refining, or reselling the item.
How Is the Gold Content of Jewelry Estimated?
A simplified way of understanding the underlying gold content is:
Net alloy weight × gold purity = approximate pure-gold weight
For example, imagine the gold alloy in a piece weighs 20 grams after accounting for stones and non-gold components, and tests as 18K.
18K gold is 75% gold.
A simplified calculation would therefore be:
20 grams × 75% = approximately 15 grams of gold content
That does
not
mean the item’s purchase offer will equal the market value of exactly 15 grams of pure gold.
Instead, it helps explain the relationship between the item’s total weight, purity, and underlying precious-metal content.
How Do Gold Buyers Test Gold?
Gold buyers may use different methods depending on the item being evaluated.
Visual Inspection and Hallmarks
An evaluator may first inspect the item for markings indicating karat or fineness.
These markings provide useful information but may still need verification.
Electronic or X-Ray Testing
Some professional buyers use electronic equipment or X-ray fluorescence technology to help analyze metal composition.
GIA research compares gold-testing methods and their limitations
. Different methods have different applications and limitations, which is why an experienced evaluator may use more than one piece of information when determining an item’s composition.
Acid Testing
Acid testing is another traditional method used to help assess gold purity.
The appropriate testing method depends on the type and condition of the item.
If you’re selling gold, you can ask the buyer
how your gold was tested and how the purity was determined
Does the Condition of Gold Jewelry Affect Its Value?
It depends on how the item is being valued.
If a broken chain is being purchased primarily for its precious-metal content, the fact that the chain is broken may matter less than its purity and gold weight.
But some jewelry may have additional resale value when it is:
Made by a desirable designer
Antique or vintage
In excellent condition
Rare
Collectible
Set with valuable gemstones
That is why potentially important jewelry shouldn’t automatically be treated as scrap.
Can Broken Gold Still Be Valuable?
Yes.
A broken gold necklace, damaged bracelet, bent ring, single earring, or other unwanted piece can still contain valuable gold.
Its precious-metal content does not disappear simply because the jewelry can no longer be worn.
If you have broken or unwanted jewelry, having it evaluated can help you understand whether it has precious-metal or additional resale value.
Are Diamonds and Gemstones Included in Gold Value?
Diamonds and gemstones should be considered separately from the gold content when they may have meaningful value.
A piece of jewelry might therefore have several potential components of value:
Consider metal content, stones, and the resale value of the complete piece without counting the same value twice.
Not every stone necessarily has significant secondary-market value, but valuable diamonds or gemstones should not automatically be ignored.
If your jewelry contains diamonds or significant gemstones, ask whether they are being evaluated separately from the gold.
Can Designer Jewelry Be Worth More Than Its Gold Content?
Yes.
Some designer, vintage, antique, collectible, or luxury jewelry can potentially be worth more as a complete piece than simply as precious metal.
Before selling potentially valuable branded jewelry, consider whether the piece has characteristics such as:
Recognizable designer markings
Original documentation
Serial numbers
Original boxes
Certificates
Historical or collectible significance
A knowledgeable evaluator should consider whether an item deserves evaluation beyond its melt or precious-metal value.
How Much Is My Gold Worth Today?
There is no single accurate answer without knowing what you have.
Determining your gold’s potential value requires information such as:
Weight
Karat or purity
Current gold market price
Whether the item contains gemstones
Brand or maker
Condition
Potential resale or collectible value
Because the gold market changes, avoid relying on an old article containing a fixed dollar amount for what gold is supposedly “worth today.”
For current market information, the
World Gold Council gold-price data
provides a useful reference.
How Can I Estimate My Gold’s Value Before Selling?
You can start by looking for the karat mark on your jewelry and getting an approximate weight.
Then check a reputable source for the current gold market price.
However, treat any home calculation as an
estimate
, not a guaranteed purchase offer.
Professional testing may determine that the item’s actual composition or weight differs from what you expected.
Additionally, jewelry with diamonds, gemstones, designer provenance, or collectible value may require a different type of evaluation.
How Can I Get a Better Offer for My Gold?
The goal shouldn’t simply be finding the buyer making the biggest advertising claim.
Instead, look for a buyer who provides a transparent evaluation.
Before selling:
Know what type of gold you have
Ask how purity was determined
Ask to understand the weight
Check the current gold market
Ask whether gemstones have separate value
Ask whether designer or collectible value was considered
Understand the offer before accepting it
If you’re comparing different ways to sell, read our guide
Where to Sell Gold in Los Angeles: How to Get the Best Price for Your Gold
Do Pawn Shops Value Gold Differently?
Different buyers can have different business models, operating costs, resale opportunities, and purchasing criteria.
That means offers for the same item may vary.
If you’re considering a pawn shop, see our guide
How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay for Gold? What Los Angeles Sellers Should Know
for a more detailed explanation.
Frequently Asked Questions About Gold Value
Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold?

Per equal unit of weight, 18K gold contains more pure gold than 14K gold. However, the total value of a specific piece also depends on its weight and potentially its design, gemstones, brand, condition, and resale value.
Is 14K gold real gold?
Yes. 14K gold is a gold alloy containing 14 parts gold out of 24 total parts. The FTC’s consumer guidance explains how karat markings indicate the proportion of gold in jewelry.
Is broken gold worth less?

If an item is being valued primarily for its precious-metal content, being broken does not eliminate the value of the gold it contains. A wearable or collectible piece, however, may have additional value based on condition.
Do gold prices change every day?

Gold prices fluctuate with market activity. For that reason, the reference price used when evaluating gold can change over time. The World Gold Council maintains gold spot-price data and related market information.
Should I sell gold based only on its weight?
No. Weight is only one part of the evaluation. Purity is crucial, and some jewelry can also have value from diamonds, gemstones, brand, craftsmanship, rarity, or collectibility.
How do I know whether a gold offer is fair?

Ask the buyer to explain the item’s tested purity, weight, market-price reference, and any other factors used in calculating the offer. Understanding those components makes comparing evaluations easier.

title: Round Brilliant Diamonds: Compare Cut Grades and Reports

body.alt: Round faceted diamond held in tweezers

children.text: Confirm shape, cutting style and report scope

Read the report’s shape and cutting-style description before comparing grades. “Round” describes an outline; an older round stone may use a different cutting arrangement from a modern round brilliant. Do not assign a grade from the name alone.
GIA’s cut-grade guide

explains the system for standard round brilliant diamonds in the D-to-Z color range. Its grades run from Excellent through Very Good, Good and Fair to Poor. That scope should not be applied automatically to every diamond shape or report type.
For another shape, ask which quality information the report does supply rather than treating the absence of the same overall cut grade as a defect.
Understand what the cut grade considers
GIA’s system considers brightness, fire, scintillation, weight ratio, durability, polish and symmetry. Its
published cut-grading research
explains why appearance, design and craftsmanship belong in the assessment.

body.alt: Loose diamonds with jeweler loupe and tweezers
body.caption: Loose diamonds with jeweler loupe and tweezers.

children.text: Brightness refers to white-light return; fire describes colored flashes; scintillation concerns sparkle and the pattern of light and dark areas. Treat these as aspects to observe together rather than expecting one photograph to show all of them.
Polish and symmetry are also reported separately. As
GIA explains
, a diamond can have an Excellent overall cut grade with Very Good polish or symmetry. Read each field instead of assuming that one grade makes all of the others identical.
Compare the same fields on both reports
Set the reports beside each other and record the following details.
GIA’s sample natural-diamond reports
provide a useful reference for the layout and terminology.

cells: Do the report number, description and presented stone match?
How do weight, diameter measurements and depth differ?
Is an overall cut grade provided, and what is it?
What does each separate finish grade say?
Are the same quality descriptions being compared?
Which report notes or later changes need explanation?

children.text: Keep report observations separate from what you learn during the current examination. Ask about a chip, abrasion, recutting or repair rather than assuming an older document answers a present-day condition question.
View the diamonds under comparable conditions

Ask to view both stones under the same lighting, at the same distance, and then under another ordinary light source. Move them gently through similar angles. This lets you compare your own impressions of brightness, contrast and appearance more consistently.

A photograph can be useful for discussion, but exposure, magnification and reflections affect what it shows. Use the picture to identify questions, and use the report and actual examination to address them. Do not infer an exact cut grade from sparkle alone.
For a mounted stone, consider how the setting affects what is visible. Compare the complete jewelry as well as the diamond rather than overlooking a loose setting or missing accent stone.
Evaluate a sale without assuming a shape premium

The round brilliant label does not establish a guaranteed resale percentage, buyer or holding-period return. Ask for a purchase offer for your actual stone and specify whether the setting and other jewelry are included.
If you have an inherited round diamond, bring the history and paperwork you possess. Ask about its cutting style before authorizing polishing, repairs or recutting. The
weight guide
and
grading-chart reference
can help organize the report details.

Does Excellent cut mean two diamonds look identical?
No. Compare the full report information and the actual stones. A shared grade is a starting point for comparison, not a guarantee of identical appearance.
Should I sell now because my diamond is round brilliant?
Shape alone is not a reason to predict a future price. Base the decision on your circumstances and a current offer for the actual item, rather than a promised investment return.

Read markings with the construction in mind

children.text: What counts as scrap gold?

Scrap gold is a useful description for gold items being considered primarily for their metal content. It can include broken chains, a damaged bracelet, a single earring, an unwanted ring, or a mixture of small jewelry pieces. An item does not need to be wearable to be brought for an evaluation.

At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, we buy scrap gold alongside complete jewelry, heavy Cuban chains and bracelets, and gold and silver coins. Bring what you actually have; the evaluation can account for the differences between individual pieces.
Separate gold purity from the weight of the whole item
The weight of a necklace or ring is not necessarily the weight of its gold.
Karat describes the proportion of gold in a gold alloy
, while a scale measures everything placed on it. Stones, clasps, inserts, and other components may need separate consideration.
Group pieces by their markings if that is easy, but do not guess at unmarked items or damage them with a home test. A buyer needs to evaluate the actual material. Our
guide to gold valuation
explains the relationship between weight, purity, and an offer.
Broken does not always mean metal value only

A broken item may still have diamonds, a maker’s signature, unusual construction, or paperwork worth discussing. Before treating a complete piece as scrap, ask how the jewelry itself and any stones are being considered.

We buy Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds. Ask how the gold and any diamonds contribute to the offer, and review the total amount for the pieces you are selling. See our

A simple list or photographs can help you keep track of the collection, but the purchase evaluation still requires the actual items. Bring any records you already have and keep similar pieces together where practical.
Compare the final offer and payment arrangements

children.text: Start with the necklace’s weight and purity
A 14K necklace contains gold alloyed with other metals. The

. To understand a metal-value estimate, you need its gold content and the weight attributable to that material. A chain’s length or width alone does not provide those figures.
Look for any markings near the clasp, but have the actual piece evaluated before relying on a karat assumption. Read
how gold is valued
for a fuller explanation of the process.
An example of gold content, not a live quote
For an illustrative calculation, 10 grams of 14K gold contains about 5.83 grams of pure gold. If pure gold were hypothetically $100 per gram, the gold content in that example would be about $583.

This calculation is an example only. It is not today’s gold price and it is not a purchase offer. It assumes the weight is gold alloy and excludes adjustments for stones, other components, and the evaluation of the actual necklace.
Cuban chains, hollow links, and complete jewelry

Two necklaces with similar dimensions can have different weights. Cuban link chains, delicate necklaces, and hollow designs need to be evaluated as the pieces they are. Ask how the buyer accounts for construction and condition.

A familiar dial logo does not authenticate a complete watch, and bright sparkle does not establish natural diamond origin. An altered watch can contain genuine components while still differing from its original configuration.

children.text: Confirm the weight and actual dimensions
A 3.5-carat diamond weighs 0.7 grams using

Use the ratio to describe shape, not certify quality

Divide the recorded length by the width to describe how elongated the oval is. A higher ratio indicates a longer outline relative to its width. Decide which outline you prefer by looking at actual examples; there is no single ratio that guarantees a pleasing result for every person or setting.

View the bow tie and light pattern in movement

The dark contrast often called a bow tie can change with viewing position and the light blocked by the observer. Inspect the oval at a normal viewing distance and move it gently. A single photograph can emphasize or hide a particular pattern.

Compare examples under similar conditions. Note whether a central dark area dominates your view and whether the appearance changes as you move. Ask for additional viewing when a photograph or short video does not show enough. Keep that visual assessment separate from the grades recorded on the report.

children.text: 1. What exact watch is being described?

Request the maker, reference and configuration. Match the description to the physical watch rather than a similar stock image. A recognizable logo or model nickname is not enough to establish the complete item.
2. What is known about the stones?
Ask whether they are identified as natural diamonds, laboratory-grown diamonds or another material, and what supports that description.
GIA discusses the examination needed to distinguish natural and laboratory-grown diamonds
Do not infer identity from sparkle. If the watch contains many stones, ask whether a stated carat weight is a documented total or an estimate. The
diamond quality factors explained by GIA
help clarify the terms without assigning a purchase price.
3. Who supplied the setting?

Separate a manufacturer gem-set configuration from a later custom bezel, dial or bracelet. Ask for records of alterations and replacement components. “Factory” in a listing should be supported, not accepted simply because the watch carries a brand name.

Check each component's material rather than assuming everything is gold. The
FTC's precious-metal terminology
distinguishes alloys from surface coatings. Whole-watch weight cannot be treated as pure-gold weight.
5. What is the present condition?

Discuss operation, known repairs, loose stones, bracelet wear and missing links. Agree before any opening, removal or further work. Do not arrange polishing or gem replacement merely because you assume it will improve resale proceeds.
6. Which records and accessories belong to it?

List the box, warranty documents, service invoices, stone reports and spare links included. A report or invoice should match the relevant watch or component. Missing records are a question to discuss, not a reason to invent its history.

Confirm the final amount, included items, unresolved inspection conditions and payment arrangements. For a purchase from a seller, read any return and warranty terms. For a sale to a buyer, distinguish an outright offer from a consignment estimate.

children.text: How a complete-piece evaluation works
Identify the selection and its records
Show which pieces are available to sell and which documents belong to each item. Explain known repairs, altered settings, replaced stones or uncertain details.
Examine materials and condition

Metal content and weight, natural diamonds, construction, wear, maker markings and supporting records can affect the proposal. Ask what has been verified and what remains uncertain. Discuss any test that could mark or alter a piece before proceeding.
Review the purchase offer

Ask whether the offer considers the complete piece or primarily its materials, which items are included and whether deductions apply. An asking price seen online is not evidence that a comparable item sold for that amount.
A preliminary estimate is not the final offer

A phone description or photograph may support an initial estimate. The final in-person offer can differ after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction, stones and other characteristics are verified. Compare final net amounts for the same selection of pieces.
What to bring and what to preserve
Complete jewelry, pairs, matching sets and detached components.
Available receipts, reports, prior appraisals, repair records and original boxes, matched to the correct item.
Your own inventory and photographs, with uncertain details identified.
A clear list of pieces you are considering selling and pieces you plan to keep.
The identification and ownership documents confirmed when arranging the visit.
Do not polish, dismantle or discard components solely to prepare a sale. A signed or antique piece may need consideration as a complete object before treating it as scrap. Our
estate jewelry inventory guide
explains how to organize the collection.
Purchase offer or formal appraisal?

A current purchase offer states what a buyer proposes to pay for specified items under stated terms. An appraisal for insurance, estate administration or tax documentation has a different purpose. Confirm the requirements with the professional requesting that document; a buyer’s informal evaluation may not satisfy them.
Before selling for an estate or another person, establish who has authority to make the decision and confirm the documents needed. Read our
inherited jewelry documentation guide
Decide what to keep and compare the same items

You can identify only the pieces you are considering selling. Separate financial considerations from sentimental decisions and ask for terms for that exact selection. A historical retail receipt or insurance replacement figure is not a promised resale payment.
Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the payment method and timing before accepting. Our guides to

Questions about selling inherited and antique jewelry
Where can I sell inherited jewelry in Los Angeles?
Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Call 310-663-1340 to describe the pieces and arrange an in-person purchase evaluation in the Downtown Jewelry District.
Is every piece of estate jewelry an antique?

No. Estate jewelry refers to previously owned pieces; inherited describes how someone received them. Neither description establishes age. An antique-style design also does not prove when a piece was made. Keep any records and describe uncertain details as unknown.
Can I bring jewelry if I do not know the stones or maker?

Yes, describe what you have when arranging a visit. Bring complete pieces and any records rather than guessing their materials or origin. Acceptance and an offer depend on the actual items and our buying scope.
Should I clean or repair antique jewelry before selling?
Keep the pieces intact and ask before cleaning, polishing, repairing or removing stones. Alterations can affect markings, surfaces, settings and other evidence needed to evaluate a complete piece.
Do I need a formal appraisal before asking for a purchase offer?

A purchase evaluation and a formal appraisal have different purposes. Bring any report you already have. If a document is needed for estate administration, insurance or another purpose, confirm its requirements with the professional requesting it.
Does an old appraisal determine the price I will receive?

No. The report’s date, purpose and description matter, and an insurance replacement figure is not a guaranteed resale payment. A current offer depends on the inspected item and the proposed purchase terms.
Can I sell only part of an inherited collection?

Identify the pieces you are considering selling and keep those you want to retain separate. Request an offer for that exact selection, and confirm your authority to sell before agreeing to a transaction.
Can a phone estimate change after the jewelry is examined?

Yes. A preliminary discussion relies on the description or photographs available. The final in-person offer can change after materials, purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction and other characteristics are verified.

Gold jewelry, scrap and coins
What gold can you sell?
Bring complete pieces, even if you think they are only worth their metal content. A maker, setting, collectible feature or natural diamond may need consideration before an item is treated as scrap.
Gold jewelry
Rings, necklaces, earrings, heavy Cuban chains and bracelets, with or without diamonds. Yellow, white and rose gold can all contain gold; color alone does not establish purity.
Broken jewelry & scrap gold
A broken clasp, damaged chain or single earring does not eliminate the gold content. Keep mixed pieces together and let the evaluation establish their purity and metal weight.
Gold coins & bullion
Bring gold coins in their holders and packaging. For bars or other bullion, call with the format and quantity before visiting so we can confirm whether we can evaluate your items.
Estate & designer jewelry
Inherited pieces and signed jewelry may have characteristics beyond melt value. Bring receipts, maker information and existing reports. Do not remove stones or polish away markings before the visit.

Understand the metal
10K, 14K, 18K, 22K and 24K gold

Karat describes the proportion of gold in an alloy. It is different from the carat weight used for diamonds. A stamp helps identify a piece, but plating, solder, repairs and mixed components can affect what is present.

cells: A higher gold proportion, still an alloy

children.text: These are purity references, not prices or guaranteed test results. Gold-plated and gold-filled items differ from solid karat gold. See the
World Gold Council's explanation of gold purity
and our
14K gold value guide
An item-specific offer
How is a cash-for-gold offer determined?

For scrap gold, a useful starting point is the weight of the gold-bearing metal multiplied by its verified gold proportion and a current pure-gold price per unit of weight. This estimates metal value; it is not a guaranteed purchase price.
Spot gold is a market reference for gold itself. Jewelry's total weight may include stones, springs or other non-gold parts. Keep grams and troy ounces consistent when comparing calculations. Our
gold valuation guide
explains the distinction.

A purchase offer can differ from theoretical metal value because of recovery or refining costs, resale potential, market conditions and the buyer's margin. Designer provenance, collectible coin features and natural diamonds need separate consideration. Ask for the final net amount and the factors behind it.
Identify and examine the items
Markings, construction, maker details and condition help establish what is being evaluated. A photograph or receipt can assist but does not replace inspecting the piece.
Check purity and weight
Ask how purity is tested, which parts are included in the weight and whether stones or non-gold components affect the calculation. Mixed karats should not be treated as one assumed purity.
Review the purchase terms
Compare the offer, any deductions and payment arrangements. A retail replacement appraisal, an online asking price and a purchase offer serve different purposes.
What should you know about gold testing?

Evaluation may involve reading hallmarks, examining construction and choosing a testing method suited to the item. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzes metal composition, but plating can affect the result. Acid or touchstone testing uses a sample or streak. Neither a marking nor one surface reading should be treated as the whole evaluation.

Ask which method will be used on your piece and whether it could leave a mark or require a sample. Discuss that first, especially for collectible coins, inherited jewelry or signed pieces. Call before visiting if you have testing concerns.
For background, GIA explains
touchstone testing
and
how plating can affect XRF results
Compare estimates carefully
A phone estimate can change after inspection

A preliminary phone or photo estimate uses details that have not yet been verified. The final in-person offer may be higher or lower after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, stones, maker details and other characteristics are checked. Market prices can also move before your visit.
Ask what assumptions an estimate uses, what remains to be checked and whether the amount is the final net purchase offer. There is no obligation to sell simply because you request an evaluation.
Discuss your gold ↗
Prepare for your visit
What should you bring when selling gold?
The complete jewelry, coins or collection you want evaluated.
Receipts, certificates, grading reports, original holders or packaging you already have.
Information about repairs, modifications, maker marks or inherited ownership.
Identification and relevant ownership or estate documents; call to confirm what is needed for your transaction.
Your questions about testing, payment method and timing.

Missing paperwork does not establish that an item has no value. Bring what you have. Do not clean collectible coins, remove gemstones or repair jewelry solely for the evaluation without discussing it first.

Questions about selling gold in Los Angeles
Where can I sell gold in Los Angeles?
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates gold at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, in the Downtown Jewelry District. Call 310-663-1340 to arrange a visit and discuss your items.
Can I sell broken jewelry or scrap gold?
Yes. We buy broken gold chains, damaged jewelry, single earrings and mixed scrap gold. An offer depends on the verified metal content and other characteristics of the actual items.
Does 18K gold always receive a higher offer than 14K?

18K has a higher nominal gold proportion per gram, but the offer also depends on weight, verified purity, stones, maker, condition and other features. A lighter 18K piece need not be worth more than a heavier 14K piece.
Do you buy gold coins and bullion?
We buy gold coins, including collections. Keep their holders and paperwork. Call ahead about bars or other bullion to confirm the format and quantity can be evaluated.
Can I sell inherited or designer gold jewelry?
Bring inherited and signed jewelry intact with available records. Discuss ownership authority when relevant. Maker, provenance, condition and stones may matter beyond gold content.
Will I receive the spot price for my jewelry?

Spot price is a reference for gold, not a guaranteed jewelry purchase price. Actual metal weight, purity, costs and other resale characteristics affect the offer. Ask for an explanation of the final net amount.
Why might my phone estimate differ from the final offer?

A phone estimate relies on unverified details. Purity, weight, authenticity, condition and other characteristics are checked in person; market conditions may also change. Compare the final offer after those checks.
Should I remove diamonds before selling gold jewelry?

Bring the complete piece first. Removing stones may damage jewelry or discard useful information. Our diamond buying covers natural, cut and polished diamonds; ask how the gold and eligible stones are considered together.

title: Website Privacy Information

children.text: Website Privacy Information
This notice explains information processed through the Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds website when you browse, contact us or use available website features.
Browsing and website security

Cloudflare helps deliver and protect this website. It processes technical request information, which can include your IP address and browser information, to provide hosting and security. If an online inquiry form is available, Cloudflare Turnstile checks for automated abuse before a message can be sent. See
Cloudflare's privacy information
This website does not offer customer account registration, a newsletter signup or an on-site payment form.
Contacting the business

You choose what to share when you call or email us. When an online inquiry form is available, it asks for your name, email address, item type and message. A phone number is optional. The form asks permission to use those details to respond to your inquiry; that permission is not a signup for marketing.

When available, the online form uses Resend to forward accepted inquiries to the business mailbox. The message includes the contact details and description you provide, along with a reference number. See
Resend's privacy information
. A message accepted by the email service is not a guarantee of inbox receipt or an appointment confirmation.

Do not include identification documents, banking information, payment-card details or other sensitive material in a website inquiry. The form does not accept file uploads. Ask the business how to provide any documents needed for a particular transaction.
Optional analytics

If Google Analytics is enabled on this website, Privacy preferences lets you choose whether to allow it. The website does not load its optional Google Analytics script before you allow analytics. Calling, emailing, opening an appointment link and sending an available inquiry do not require analytics consent.

When you allow analytics, it helps the business understand page visits and contact actions. The website's own contact-action events include the action and the site page, without the name, email address, phone number or message entered in the inquiry form. Google can also process browser, device and cookie information. See
Google's privacy policy

These website analytics controls keep advertising storage and personalized advertising off. Opening an appointment link is measured as a click, not a confirmed booking; a form acceptance is not measured as confirmed inbox delivery.
Changing your browser preferences

Open Privacy preferences to change or withdraw your analytics choice. Rejecting optional analytics keeps it off. Withdrawing an earlier permission disables optional analytics on the current page and clears the accessible analytics cookies used by this setup. When the saved choice can be updated or removed, the page reloads to stop the loaded analytics script. If browser storage prevents both, analytics stays off on the current page and a notice explains that the choice applies only to that page. You can remove the earlier saved choice in your browser settings.

Your saved analytics choice is valid for up to 180 days. After it expires, analytics stays off until you choose to allow it again. If browser storage is unavailable, the page explains that your choice applies only to that page. You can also remove this site's saved browser data using your browser settings.

The menu can separately remember whether you choose sounds on or off. This preference does not require your name or contact details. Change it using the menu sound control or clear this site's saved browser data.
How long information is kept
We keep customer inquiries only as long as needed to answer questions and complete transactions, and we delete them upon request. All privacy and deletion requests are handled by the owner.

The 180-day analytics preference period describes how long a saved permission remains valid. It does not describe how long inquiry messages, business records or service-provider data are retained, and it does not automatically delete the saved browser record.
Appointment links and other services
Phone and email links open your device's calling or email service. Appointment links can open Calendly, where you choose the information to provide. Review
Calendly's privacy notice
before using its scheduling service.
Maps, social profiles and other external links take you to services with their own privacy practices. The contact choices on this website do not change the privacy settings of those services.
Questions and requests
To ask about information you have shared with Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, or to request a correction or removal, email
cash4goldanddiamond@gmail.com
, call
, or write to 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Describe your request and the contact method you used. Do not send unnecessary sensitive documents.

children.text: Our buying focus
Large stones. Exceptional color. Individual evaluation.
We focus on large, high-quality gemstones, loose or in fine jewelry. These examples reflect our interests; describe your stone so we can discuss whether an evaluation is appropriate.
Colombian emeralds
Large green emeralds with quality, condition and any known treatments considered together.
Burmese rubies
High-quality, substantial rubies, including stones described as originating in Burma, now Myanmar.
Ceylon blue sapphires
Large, high-quality blue sapphires, including Sri Lankan stones traditionally described as Ceylon.
Reports optional
Bring existing certificates and records if available. You can request an evaluation without them.
Bring the complete piece and what you know
Share the known weight or dimensions, condition, setting and any treatment or origin information. Keep estimates and family descriptions distinct from laboratory findings.
Do not remove a mounted stone or arrange aggressive cleaning to prepare the visit. Bring any report, receipt or repair record you already have.
Describe your gemstone
Tell us about its size, appearance and the jewelry it belongs to, if any.
Discuss the evaluation
We consider the actual stone, its quality, condition and supporting information. An origin claim alone does not guarantee an offer.
Review the purchase terms
Confirm which items the offer includes and your preferred payment arrangement before deciding.
Natural diamonds have a separate scope
Any diamond size. Any diamond shape.
We buy natural, cut and polished diamonds of any size or shape, loose or in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.

Gemstone selling questions
Which gemstones do you buy?
We buy only large, high-quality gemstones, including green Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies and Ceylon blue sapphires. Certificates are welcome but not required.
Do I need a gemstone certificate?
No. A certificate or laboratory report is welcome but is not required to request an evaluation. Bring the stone or complete jewelry and whatever information you already have.
Can color prove a gemstone’s origin?
No. Share the source of an origin description, such as a laboratory report, receipt or family history. The actual stone needs examination; appearance alone does not establish geographic origin.
Does the gemstone size requirement apply to diamonds?
We buy natural, cut and polished diamonds of any size or shape, loose or in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.
How can I receive payment?
Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the final amount and payment arrangements before accepting.

title: How to Check a Rolex: Why Visual Tests Cannot Authenticate It

body.alt: Two-tone Rolex Yacht-Master with white dial
body.caption: Two-tone Rolex Yacht-Master with white dial.

children.text: Use photographs to identify questions

Compare the claimed reference with reliable manufacturer information, but do not assume that a current catalog contains every older configuration. Ask about an apparent mismatch instead of declaring a watch genuine or counterfeit from one feature.
A photograph may hide movement details, later parts or damage. A familiar-looking dial does not authenticate the whole timepiece, and an unusual configuration may require historical research.
Do not rely on simple pass-or-fail tests

Weight varies with material, bracelet length and configuration. Hand motion, lens appearance and engraving cannot independently establish authenticity. A copied identifying number can appear convincing while proving nothing about the item carrying it.

Water resistance is not an authenticity test. Never immerse a watch to find out whether it is genuine. Do not scratch metal, force controls or use improvised tools to expose numbers or remove components.
Distinguish different kinds of replacement

Ask separately about original components, manufacturer service replacements, aftermarket parts and suspected counterfeit components. A later part does not automatically explain the status of every other part in the watch.

body.alt: Two-tone Rolex Daytona with black dial
body.caption: Two-tone Rolex Daytona with black dial.

children.text: For a vintage example, the
vintage Rolex guide
covers records and originality. For gem-set watches, a diamond bezel also raises separate questions about stone identity and the source of the setting; see the
diamond watch guide
Match records to the actual item
Bring warranty papers, purchase records and service invoices. Check that their descriptions and identifying information correspond to the watch. A box or card alone is not proof of authenticity.
Record known repairs and explain missing history honestly. Do not buy unrelated paperwork to make a watch appear to have documented provenance.
Agree on a suitable examination

Ask the professional what will be examined, whether the case must be opened, what conclusions can be documented and what limitations remain. Give permission before proposed work and obtain an item record if the watch must be left.
Rolex provides official servicing information
. Its
Certified Pre-Owned programme
is a specific brand programme; an independent purchase evaluation is not automatically a Rolex-issued guarantee or a formal authentication report.
If you are considering a sale
Use the
Rolex selling checklist
to organize the complete watch and accessories. Raise authenticity concerns before discussing a final purchase amount, and do not present an uncertain watch as authenticated.

at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call
to arrange an evaluation. Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases; confirm the payment arrangements before accepting.
